title: xAI ships long-term memory in Grok Build for developer sessions
subtitle: A new memory layer stores project decisions across sessions and adds /memory and /dream commands, aimed at closing the coding-agent context gap.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: xAI launched a long-term memory feature for Grok Build, its developer-facing coding harness, on September 16, 2026. The feature persists key decisions and factual context across sessions, filters out temporary and sensitive material at write time, and exposes two new commands: /memory to inspect and edit what has been stored, and /dream to compact the store and generate summary artifacts. The launch shipped alongside faster session startup, richer image handling, configurable rate-limit retries, and a set of composer usability fixes.

The problem being solved is real and specific to coding agents. A developer working with Claude Code, Codex, or Grok Build spends the first several minutes of every new session re-explaining the same context: the repository layout, the architectural decisions, the naming conventions, why a particular library was ruled out three weeks ago. Every one of those tokens is repeated work the model does not remember. A memory layer that a developer can inspect and edit is the difference between a coding assistant that resets each morning and one that accumulates a working model of the project — closer to how a human collaborator behaves after a few weeks on a team.

The competitive frame: OpenAI shipped a memory feature for ChatGPT users in 2024, Anthropic added durable projects to Claude in 2025, and Cursor and Windsurf have each shipped some form of persistent workspace context this year. xAI is later than several of them but is shipping into Grok Build's developer surface first, where the value is highest and the failure modes are the most inspectable. The one to watch is what data leaks between projects and users: memory features become privacy incidents fast when the filter that decides what is "temporary or sensitive" gets a call wrong.

Takeaway for learners: if you are building an application on top of an LLM, memory is now table stakes and you should understand the tradeoffs before your users start expecting one. Read the OpenAI and Anthropic memory docs to see two different design philosophies; sketch a schema for what you would store, when you would write to it, and how a user would edit and delete entries. The teams that get memory right will pull ahead in agent products over the next 12 months, and the ones that do not will look brittle by comparison.
